section_1.title: Introduction: The 'Life Guard' Problem
section_1.content: Introduce refraction by framing it as an optimization problem: a lifeguard on a sandy beach needs to reach a swimmer in the water as fast as possible. Since running on sand is slower than swimming in water, the lifeguard must choose an angle that minimizes total travel time.
section_1.example: Visual animation showing a lifeguard choosing a straight line (short distance, long time in sand) vs. an angled path (longer distance, shorter time in sand).

section_2.title: Prerequisite Geometry: Defining the Interface
section_2.content: Establish the coordinate system: two media with refractive indices n1 and n2, separated by a flat boundary. Define incident angle (θ1) and refracted angle (θ2) relative to the normal line.
section_2.example: A split-screen graphic: Top half is air (n1), bottom half is water (n2), with a dashed vertical 'normal' line intersecting the boundary.

section_3.title: Mathematical Formulation of Time
section_3.content: Express the total time (T) as a function of distance and speed (v = c/n). T = (d1 / v1) + (d2 / v2). Introduce the variable 'x' as the distance along the boundary to the refraction point.
section_3.example: An interactive diagram where moving the refraction point 'x' updates the equation T(x) in real-time.

section_4.title: Deriving Snell’s Law via Fermat's Principle
section_4.content: Apply Fermat’s Principle of Least Time: take the derivative of T(x) with respect to x and set it to zero (dT/dx = 0). Show the resulting geometric relationship between the sines of the angles.
section_4.example: Step-by-step mathematical expansion: dT/dx = (sinθ1 / v1) - (sinθ2 / v2) = 0, leading directly to n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2.

section_5.title: Conclusion: Real-world Synthesis
section_5.content: Summarize how the proof demonstrates that light 'chooses' the path of least time. Relate this back to the lifeguard analogy to solidify the conceptual intuition.
section_5.example: Show a laser beam bending through a glass block side-by-side with the lifeguard's path to demonstrate the universal nature of the law.
